data.restaurants.troodos-square.parking: Square and visitor centre; fills at weekends.
data.restaurants.troodos-square.winterTi: Post-hike warmth. Hot chocolate, coffee. Snow possible—cosy inside. Essential after Artemis or Atalante.
data.restaurants.zygi-mikri.description: Zygi's smaller marina and back-street spots. Less touristy than the main harbour. Fresh fish, meze. Winter Sunday lunch—locals' ritual. Combine with Choirokoitia, Lefkara, or Governor's Beach. The pace is slow.
data.restaurants.zygi-mikri.localSecret: Mikri marina. The locals' Zygi. Slow pace, fresh fish.
data.restaurants.zygi-mikri.name: Zygi Mikri Marina
data.restaurants.zygi-mikri.winterTip: Back-street Zygi. Locals' Sunday. Less touristy.
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.bestTimeT: Lunch; Sundays especially busy with locals
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.descripti: Between Larnaca and Limassol. No ruins, no lace. Just fish. The tavernas line the harbour; they serve what the boats brought in that morning. Locals eat here. Winter lunch on the waterfront—octopus, sea bream, calamari. The pace is slow. The coffee after is obligatory. Zygi is where Cypriots go for Sunday fish. Combine with Choirokoitia, Lefkara, or Cape Greco trail.
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.localSecr: Between Larnaca and Limassol. No ruins, no lace. Just fish. The pace is slow. The coffee after is obligatory.
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.name: Zygi Fish Tavernas
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.transport: Zygi harbour, between Larnaca and Limassol. ~25 min from Larnaca.
data.restaurants.zygi-tavernas.winterTip: The tavernas line the harbour. Order what the boats brought in. Sunday is locals' day. Combine with Choirokoitia or Lefkara.
data.secretGems.adonis-polis-loop.body: Do the trail in the morning. Finish by 1pm. Drive to Polis for lunch. The harbour tavernas serve fish that's fresh. Vasilikon winery is on the Akamas loop back. Or skip the wine and just eat. The trail earns you the meal. Polis knows how to feed hikers. Two days if you can: hike, eat, sleep, repeat.
data.secretGems.adonis-polis-loop.title: Adonis or Aphrodite, then Polis
data.secretGems.amiantos-geopark-first.b: Watch the Geopark documentary first. Then the geological garden—rocks in stratigraphic order. Then trails into recovering pine. The mine school building is the point. €3. Winter snow sometimes. Honest industrial heritage.
data.secretGems.amphorae-history-dive.bo: Boat from Paphos harbour. Roman jars on the cave ceiling at 12 metres. Winter visibility often beats summer. The amphorae are protected—look, don't touch. Ask about turtles on the Moulia loop. 5mm wetsuit Dec to Feb.
data.secretGems.artemis-psilo-dendro.bod: Do Artemis in the morning. Finish by 1pm. Then drive to Platres and eat at Psilo Dendro taverna—the one by the river. The owner knows every hiker. Order the trout with almonds. The fireplace, the mountain air. It's the pairing locals do. Don't skip it.
data.secretGems.asinou-before-museum.bod: See Panagia tis Asinou at Nikitari first—1105, Comnenian frescoes in the nave. Then Cyprus Museum in Nicosia. The museum panels make sense once you've stood in the original. Weekday mornings, you might have the church alone.
data.secretGems.athalassa-botanical-firs: Free botanical garden at the main gate—do it first. Then the lake trail counter-clockwise. Most people stop at the café. You get an hour of quiet pine before Nicosia traffic calls you back.
data.secretGems.avakas-post-hike.body: Do the gorge in the morning. The narrowest point—where the sky becomes a strip—go slow. When you're done, call Avakas Winery. They're used to hikers. The Xynisteri from mountain vines has a different character. Ask. They'll tell you. Ten minutes by car from the trailhead.
data.secretGems.avakas-post-hike.title: Avakas Gorge, then Avakas Winery
data.secretGems.bellapais-tree.body: Durrell wrote that sitting under it made you lazy. He was right. In Bellapais square, order a coffee under the tree. A winter afternoon there is tradition. The abbey is above you. The village below. Don't rush. The tree has been there for centuries. It can wait.
data.secretGems.bellapais-tree.title: The Tree of Idleness
data.secretGems.cape-greco-konnos.body: Walk the Cape Greco Coastal Path in the morning. Drop down to Konnos Bay for a break—white sand, emerald water. In winter you might have it to yourself. Bring a wind layer; the cliffs funnel the breeze. Protaras or Fig Tree Bay for lunch. The trail earns the beach.
data.secretGems.cape-greco-konnos.title: Cape Greco: trail then Konnos
data.secretGems.choirokoitia-mist.body: Winter mornings can be misty. Go early. The hilltop settlement feels suspended between past and present. Seven thousand years. The defensive wall makes sense from the top. Climb there first. The reconstructed dwellings, the round houses—you'll see the layout. Allow an hour and a half. Then Lefkara for lace and lunch. Or the Cyprus Museum in Nicosia for context. Choirokoitia deserves the morning.
data.secretGems.choirokoitia-mist.title: Choirokoitia: misty morning
data.secretGems.domes-atupon.body: Atypon means 'unexpected'—ask about it. Their Atypon 02 (Assyrtiko & Xynisteri) and Rosé Maratheftiko 2024 surprise people who think they know Cypriot wine. Skarinou is a short drive from Larnaca or Limassol. Indigenous varieties only. Can't visit? Order from their online shop. Book tastings ahead.
data.secretGems.domes-atupon.title: Domes Sergiou: the Atypon range
data.secretGems.episkopi-winter-sun.body: When Gerakopetra is freezing, Episkopi south face catches January sun. Start 11am. Lower overhangs dry faster after rain. Zambartas winery on the way down. The Paphos climber's weekday secret.
data.secretGems.eptagoneia-kafenion-beta: Locals know which limestone blocks dry first after rain—the east-facing ones by Kellaki road. Coffee first. Then a half-day on rock between Klirou and Arakapas without the Laona drive.
data.secretGems.fikardou-square.body: The village was nearly abandoned. Now it's a living museum. You can walk it in twenty minutes. Give yourself an hour. Stand in the square. Listen. The wooden balconies. The stone. The Pitsilia region rolls away. The museum key lives at the Folk Art Museum—ask there. The Rural Life Museum tells how mountain families survived. Step back. The silence is the gift.
data.secretGems.fikardou-square.title: Fikardou: stand in the square
data.secretGems.foini-potters.body: Foini is known for pottery. The workshops are in the village. Ask at any shop—they'll point you. Watch a potter at the wheel. The smell of clay and wood smoke. They're proud of the craft. It's not a show; it's how they work. Quieter than Omodos. The village has a different rhythm. Combine with Platres or a Troodos trail. Foini rewards the curious. Give yourself a morning.
data.secretGems.foini-potters.title: Foini: watch a potter
data.secretGems.governors-beach-cliffs.b: White cliffs above dark volcanic sand. On a mild December afternoon you can sit outside with a blanket. The fish is fresh. Do Kourion or Kolossi in the morning, fish at lunch. Fifteen minutes from Kourion. Zambartas winery is an easy add-on. The contrast—white cliffs, dark sand—is striking in winter light.
data.secretGems.governors-beach-cliffs.t: Governor's Beach: white cliffs, dark sand
data.secretGems.governors-coves.body: The coast has a string of coves. Don't stop at the first. Drive along. Find a pocket. The white cliffs, the dark volcanic sand—the contrast is striking in winter light. On a mild December afternoon, the cliff tavernas do lunch. Sit outside with a blanket. The fish is fresh. Amathus and Kourion are fifteen minutes away. Ruins in the morning, fish at lunch. The coast rewards the patient.
data.secretGems.governors-coves.title: Governor's Beach: find your cove
data.secretGems.green-bay-turtle-rock.bo: Prasinada Bay. Walk-in shore dive or snorkel. The fish rock is centre bay; turtles often cruise the seagrass on the east side. Winter visibility beats summer. 5mm wetsuit. Morning before wind picks up.
data.secretGems.green-bay-turtle-rock.ti: Green Bay: east side for turtles
data.secretGems.ineia-kafenion-intel.bod: Before Gerakopetra, stop at Ineia square. Order coffee. Ask if the gravel track is dry. The kafenion knows. Climbers who skip this step sometimes turn back muddy. The village also has the last loo before the crag. Small things matter.
data.secretGems.ineia-kafenion-intel.tit: Ineia kafenion: ask about the road
data.secretGems.kakopetria-psarovrasto.b: Trout poached in wine and herbs. The tavernas line the Kryos Potamos. Do Caledonia or Kryos Potamos loop in the morning, Kakopetria for lunch. Galata's UNESCO painted churches are nearby—allow time to wander. Fireplace, mountain air. Kakopetria knows hikers. Psaróvrasto is the order.
data.secretGems.kalavasos-tenta-first.bo: Tenta Neolithic site—7,000 years, domed structures, open in winter. Do it before Lefkara lace. The contrast matters. Zygi fish lunch on the coast after. Mild corridor between Larnaca and Limassol.
data.secretGems.kalopanagiotis-springs.b: Everyone visits the Venetian bridge. The thermal springs are at the edge of the village—ask at the museum or any local. A soak in winter feels like a gift. The valley is cold, the water is warm. Go early. The bridge after. Lampadistis church. In that order.
data.secretGems.kalopanagiotis-springs.t: The thermal springs before the bridge
data.secretGems.kato-platres-trout.body: Do Artemis or Caledonia from Platres in the morning. Skip the square crowds. Eat at Psilo Dendro in Kato Platres—trout by the river, fire going. The sound of the Kryos Potamos. Locals' pairing.
data.secretGems.kato-platres-trout.title: Kato Platres: river after the trail
data.secretGems.kiti-angeloktisti.body: Kiti village, near Larnaca airport. The church of Angeloktisti—built by angels, the legend says—holds a 6th-century mosaic of the Virgin and Child. One of the oldest surviving Byzantine mosaics in the eastern Mediterranean. Most tour buses skip it. The village is quiet. The church is small, intimate. Allow forty minutes. Combine with Zygi for fish lunch, or Larnaca. It's the kind of detour that changes your sense of the island.
data.secretGems.kiti-angeloktisti.title: Kiti: the church the buses miss
data.secretGems.kolios-meze-cash.body: The meze at Kolios isn't tourist meze—it's village food, cooked by the owner's wife. Authentic. Book one or two days ahead. February is quiet; you'll have the mountain views and the cellar mostly to yourself. They may not take cards—bring cash. The wine is €5–14 at the cellar, well below retail. The Iris white, from the rare Spourtiko grape, is a standout. Chrysorrogiatissa is ten minutes away; do both in a morning.
data.secretGems.kolios-meze-cash.title: Kolios: book the lunch, bring cash
data.secretGems.kolossi-sugar-mill.body: Everyone pays for the castle. The sugar mill ruins beside it are free. Walk over. Commandaria was made here for eight hundred years. The stones are atmospheric. Rarely crowded. Do the castle first—climb to the roof. Then the ruins. Pair with Zambartas (Limassol) or Kolios (Paphos hills) for a tasting. Thirty minutes at Kolossi. The rest of the afternoon for wine.
data.secretGems.kolossi-sugar-mill.title: Kolossi: the free bit
data.secretGems.kormakitis-maronite.body: North Cyprus. Kormakitis is one of four Maronite villages—Arabic-speaking Cypriots who've been here since the 12th century. The church, the square, the sense of a culture that has survived. It's not on the main tourist loop. You need a car. But if you're exploring the north—Bellapais, St Hilarion, Kyrenia—add Kormakitis. The village speaks a different Cyprus. Winter mornings are quiet. The light on the stone is worth the drive.
data.secretGems.kouklia-cafe.body: Palaipafos sits in the village. There's a café. Order a coffee. The ruins are over your shoulder. The pace here is slower than Paphos harbour. Fewer tour buses. The temple of Aphrodite, the Roman mosaics—they're right there. Sit. The village doesn't rush. Neither should you.
data.secretGems.kouklia-cafe.title: Kouklia: the café with the ruins
data.secretGems.kourion-bench-lunch.body: There's a bench at the far edge of the theatre facing the sea. Go at 4pm in December—the light hits the ruins. You'll have it to yourself on a weekday. Then Episkopi village for meze. Kourion in the morning, Episkopi for lunch. Governor's Beach is fifteen minutes away if you want fish instead.
data.secretGems.kourion-bench.body: Nobody talks about the bench that faces the sea. It's at the far edge of the theatre, looking down over the bay. Go at 4pm in December. The light hits the ruins, the coast glows. You'll have it to yourself on a weekday. Governor's Beach is fifteen minutes away—ruins in the morning, fish at lunch.
data.secretGems.kourion-bench.title: The bench at Kourion
data.secretGems.kritou-terra-akamas.body: Before Polis, before the Baths of Aphrodite. Kritou Terra sits in the hills above the Akamas. A few hundred people. A kafenion. No tour buses. The views run down to the coast. Stop for a coffee if you're driving to Lara or the Adonis trailhead. The village doesn't expect you. That's the point. The road through is scenic. Take it slow.
data.secretGems.kyperounta-fire-tower.bo: At km 2.5 on the Madari Ridge trail, there's a fire watchtower. Climb it if you can. The 360° views are worth the extra steps. Kyperounta Winery is nearby—among Europe's highest wineries by altitude. Combine the trail with a tasting. Call ahead. They're used to hikers. The valley light in winter is golden. Don't skip the tower.
data.secretGems.kyperounta-snow.body: At 1,400m Kyperounta is among Europe's highest wineries by facility altitude—Tsiakkas's Petralona vineyard reaches higher still. Call ahead in Jan–Feb—snow can close the road. December or March are safer. Wrap up warm; the tasting room has heaters but the drive up is half the adventure. Combine with Olympus Summit or Artemis trail. The high-altitude wines have minerality you won't find at sea level.
data.secretGems.kyperounta-snow.title: Kyperounta: Europe's highest
data.secretGems.lagoudera-araka-key.body: Panagia tou Araka—1192 frescoes, among the finest Komnenian work on the island. Key from the village. Short steep walk. See it before lunch in Kakopetria. Dress modestly. Winter cloud in the valley; the church often clear above.
data.secretGems.laiki-geitonia-market.bo: Nicosia's old town. Laiki Geitonia is the restored neighbourhood—narrow streets, craft shops, cafés. Fewer tour groups than Ledra. Wander. Find the market street. In winter the light hits the stone. Combine with Leventis or the buffer zone crossing. It's where locals still shop for herbs and honey. The kind of place that feels lived-in, not staged.
data.secretGems.laiki-geitonia-market.ti: Laiki Geitonia: the old town market
data.secretGems.lara-picnic.body: No sunbeds. No bars. Raw coast. Pack a picnic, bring water. In winter the turtles are gone and the beach is empty. You might see no one for hours. 4WD recommended for the access road. The golden sand, the turquoise water—this is the Akamas. Bring it with you. Leave nothing.
data.secretGems.lara-picnic.title: Lara Beach: pack a picnic
data.secretGems.larnaca-cycle-tochni-sta: Park at Tochni square, roll toward Kalavasos and down to Zygi for lunch. Reverse the loop if the wind is off the sea. Forty kilometres, mostly quiet. Tenta ruins if you have thirty minutes to spare.
Closer to the Baths of Aphrodite trailhead than Polis. Simpler, quieter. Do Adonis or Aphrodite in the morning, Latsi for lunch before the loop back. Fresh fish, harbour views. The drive along the coast is part of the day. Less crowded than Polis harbour. Vasilikon winery on the loop home.
data.secretGems.ledra-buffer-zone.body: The pedestrian crossing into the buffer zone. Mid-morning, 11am, the light is soft and the queues are shorter. Walk through. The empty shops, the UN posts, the line painted on the ground. It takes five minutes. The weight of it stays. Combine with Leventis or a Ledra café. Don't rush the crossing. It matters.
data.secretGems.ledra-buffer-zone.title: Ledra Street: cross at 11am
data.secretGems.lefkara-kato.body: Everyone goes to Pano Lefkara first. Start in Kato Lefkara instead—the lower village. Quieter. The lacemakers sit in doorways. Fewer tour groups. Walk up to Pano when you're ready. The silver shops are in both. Kato has the pace.
data.secretGems.lefkara-kato.title: Skip Pano. Start in Kato.
data.secretGems.leventis-first.body: Most visitors head straight to the Cyprus Museum. Go to Leventis first. It's free, intimate, tells Nicosia's story in a way the big museum can't. Two hours. Then Cyprus Museum. The context will make Kourion, Pafos, Choirokoitia come alive. On a rainy day: Leventis, then a café on Ledra Street. You'll thank yourself.
data.secretGems.leventis-first.title: Leventis before Cyprus Museum
data.secretGems.lofou-before-omodos.body: Lofou sits above Omodos on the wine route. Fewer tour buses. Stone houses, a quiet square, and kafenions that locals actually use. Stop for a coffee on the way to or from Omodos. The village doesn't perform. It just is. Winter weekday mornings you might have the square to yourself. Krasas winery and Monagri are nearby. The road between Lofou and Omodos is one of the prettiest in the Krasochoria.
data.secretGems.louvaras-before-omodos.b: On the Limassol–Troodos wine route. Louvaras is quieter than Omodos. Stop for a coffee first. The kafenions know how to welcome strangers. Then work up to Omodos and Koilani. Or do it backwards. Louvaras doesn't shout. It waits. The stone holds the sun in winter.
Weekday mornings before 10am—calm bay, clear patches for snorkel or SUP. The kite schools arrive when the wind builds. Finikoudes pier first if you want a longer walk; Mackenzie for the paddle. Zenobia boats leave from the marina, not here.
data.secretGems.marina-far-end.body: Everyone clusters near the entrance. Walk to the far end, toward the old fort. Fewer tourists, same views. The superyachts, the water. Order a coffee first. Sit. Let the marina settle. Then choose a restaurant. Don't rush the approach. The promenade rewards the walk. In winter the light hits the water at four.
data.secretGems.marina-far-end.title: The far end of the marina
data.secretGems.millomeris-platres.body: Do Millomeris in the morning. Short trail. The waterfall. Finish by noon. Drive to Platres. The trout tavernas or a café by the river. It's a gentle half-day. Ideal when you don't want a full mountain push. The village knows hikers. Order the trout with almonds. The fireplace. The mountain can wait.
data.secretGems.millomeris-platres.title: Millomeris, then Platres lunch
data.secretGems.nissi-winter-coffee.body: One of the beach cafés stays open all winter. The one with the wooden deck. Order a coffee. Sit. The rock islet, the horizon, the empty sand. In summer you'd never get a seat. December? You might be the only one. The light is different. Take it.
data.secretGems.nissi-winter-coffee.titl: Nissi in winter: the café that stays open
data.secretGems.omodos-blue-door.body: In Omodos square, there's a kafenion with a blue door—the one the winemakers use. Order a Greek coffee. Sit. The zivania is better here than in the tourist spots. Winter mornings, the stove is lit and the village hasn't woken yet. Don't rush.
data.secretGems.omodos-blue-door.title: The kafenion with the blue door
data.secretGems.omodos-tavernas-blue-doo: In Omodos square, there's a kafenion with a blue door—the one the winemakers use. Order a Greek coffee. Sit. The zivania is better here than in the tourist spots. Winter mornings, the stove is lit. After Tsiakkas or Artemis, Omodos is the natural lunch stop. Meze, wine, the pace of the village. Reserve weekends.
Omodos: the kafenion with the blue door
data.secretGems.pafos-far-cafe.body: The café at the far end of the harbour, past the castle. Tuesday 3pm. You'll have the sunset to yourself. The fishing boats, the stone, the light. In summer it's packed. Winter? Empty. Order a coffee. Stay until five.
data.secretGems.pafos-far-cafe.title: Paphos harbour, the far café
data.secretGems.palaipafos-kouklia.body: Aphrodite's sanctuary. Winter ruins, quieter than the main Pafos mosaics. Kouklia village wraps around the site. Stop for a coffee—the ruins are over your shoulder. Tomb of Kings and Pafos harbour are a short drive. The pace here is slower. The village doesn't expect you. That's the point.
data.secretGems.palaipafos-kouklia.title: Palaipafos: Kouklia for coffee
data.secretGems.polis-harbour-trail.body: Do Adonis or Aphrodite in the morning. Finish by 1pm. Polis harbour for lunch. The tavernas serve what the boats brought in. Vasilikon winery is on the loop back. Two days if you can: hike, eat, sleep, repeat. The harbour knows hikers. Order what's fresh.
data.secretGems.polis-harbour-trail.titl: Polis: the trail earns the meal
data.secretGems.pomos-pier-snorkel.body: When the sea is flat, the fish shelter under the stone pier. Reef shoes, mask, winter wetsuit or thick rash vest. The harbour is working—respect the boats. Midweek morning, you might share the water with one fisherman mending nets. Post-paddle coffee at the van by the beach.
data.secretGems.pomos-pier-snorkel.title: Pomos pier: snorkel the harbour wall
data.secretGems.psilo-dendro-trout.body: The one by the river. Order the trout with almonds—psaróvrasto, poached in wine and herbs. The owner knows every hiker. Do Artemis or Caledonia in the morning; finish by 1pm. Drive to Platres. The fireplace, the mountain air. It's the pairing locals do. Don't skip it.
data.secretGems.psilo-dendro-trout.title: Psilo Dendro: trout with almonds
data.secretGems.rainy-nicosia.body: When the mountains are wet and the coast is grey, Nicosia works. Leventis first—free, intimate. Then Cyprus Museum—nine thousand years. Then a café on Ledra Street. The buffer zone crossing if you're up for it. The old town. You can spend a full day indoors and still feel like you've seen Cyprus. The rain outside fades. The galleries hold you.
data.secretGems.rainy-nicosia.title: Rainy day: Nicosia
data.secretGems.santo-sunset.body: Book lunch for 12–2; in winter the terrace fills at weekends. Sunset in December is around 5pm—time it right and you get the golden hour with a glass. Their Ayios Onoufrios red pairs well with meze. On a mild day you can sit outside with a blanket. Kourion and Governor's Beach are nearby for a full Limassol coast day.
data.secretGems.santo-sunset.title: Santo: time the sunset
data.secretGems.sea-caves-afternoon.body: The limestone glows amber when the sun is low. Go after 3pm in winter. The angle of the light hits the arches. Bring a wind layer—the cliffs catch the breeze. In summer it's packed. December? You might have the caves to yourself. Combine with Konnos Bay: walk the coastal path, drop down for a coffee. The light does the rest.
data.secretGems.silikou-valley-morning.b: Drive in when fog fills the Commandaria valley. Wait twenty minutes at the museum café. The terraces appear. Walk toward Doros. Savvas winery if you called ahead. Omodos can wait.
data.secretGems.solea-valley-trout.body: Kakopetria, Galata, Kalopanagiotis. Trout, meze, river settings, fireplaces. Do Mylikouri or Kampos tou Livadiou in the morning, then Kakopetria or Galata for lunch. Psaróvrasto is the classic. The valley rewards slow drives. Cosy in winter. Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis is on the loop.
data.secretGems.solea-valley-trout.title: Solea Valley: trout by the fire
data.secretGems.st-hilarion-window.body: In the lower ward, there's a window that frames the sea. It's the shot. Get there early—before 10am—and you might have it to yourself. The castle climbs; the Queen's Window is worth the steps. The coast spreads out below. Kyrenia, the harbour, the horizon. Dress in layers. The wind never stops. But the window? Worth the steps.
data.secretGems.st-hilarion-window.title: St Hilarion: the Queen's Window
data.secretGems.statos-village-wine.body: Statos is a wine village. Chrysorrogiatissa monastery is nearby. But the village itself—stone houses, a square, a kafenion—gets overlooked. Stop. Walk. The pace is slower than Omodos or Koilani. Tria Elit winery is here. The village feeds into the wine; the wine doesn't define the village. Winter light. Silence. The kind of place you find when you're not looking.
data.secretGems.statos-village-wine.titl: Statos: the village behind the wine
data.secretGems.the-farmyard-akamas.body: Wiz 50 Best top 5. Ethnic Asian comfort in Kathikas. Do Adonis or Aphrodite in the morning, then book lunch. Reserve 1–2 days ahead; weekends fill. Vasilikon and Sygkrasi wineries are minutes away. The Akamas trails earn you this meal. The village setting and the food make it a destination.
One night is a pause. Two nights is when Tochni works. Cook in the guesthouse kitchen. Walk the 2.8 km trail at dusk. Choirokoitia by day, village silence by evening. The golden stone catches fire at 4pm in December.
data.secretGems.tomb-of-kings-light.body: The underground tombs stay cool. In winter the contrast with the mild coastal air is striking. Go mid-morning if you want the tombs first. Or late afternoon: the light on the stone, the shadows long. The site closes at 5pm in winter. Get there by 3:30. You'll have an hour and a half. The scale hits differently when the sun is low.
data.secretGems.tomb-of-kings-mosaics.bo: Do the tombs in the morning; the light casts long shadows in the chambers. Allow an hour. Then Pafos mosaics or harbour for lunch. The Tomb of the Kings sits north of the harbour; the mosaics and castle are fifteen minutes away. Winter is atmospheric—cool underground, mild above. Pair with Kouklia village for a slower pace.
data.secretGems.tomb-of-kings-mosaics.ti: Tombs of the Kings: then the mosaics
data.secretGems.troodos-square-warmth.bo: After Artemis, Atalante, or Persephone. Hot chocolate, coffee, sandwiches. Snow possible—cosy inside. The square is the Troodos hub. Essential post-hike warmth. Olympus ski resort is nearby when snow falls. Simple, no fuss. The mountains do the work; Troodos Square restores you.
data.secretGems.tsangarides-organic.body: The family has made wine in Lemona for over a century; commercial since 2005. Mattaro 2005 and Cabernet 2005 both won gold. Mon–Sat 9–5; closed Sunday. Their Agios Efrem red (Grenache, Mataro, Shiraz) is worth asking about. Part of the Laona route; combine with Vouni Panayia and Chrysorrogiatissa for a full Paphos hills day.
data.secretGems.tsiakkas-heights.body: Their Petralona vineyard at 1,460m is among the highest in Europe. Ask about it. The Promara 2020 was voted one of Decanter's 100 best wines in the world. Book a tour at 12:00 or 14:00—the terrace has heaters in winter. Pelendri village; combine with Artemis trail or Omodos. The family often pours; they'll point you to the best halloumi in the village.
data.secretGems.tsiakkas-heights.title: Tsiakkas: the vineyard at 1,460 metres
data.secretGems.tzelefos-dawn.body: The bridge before 9am in winter. Mist on the Diarizos, moss wet, no one else. Park at Agios Nikolaos and walk down. The arch in grey light is worth the early start. Milia lodge does breakfast if you stayed. If not, drive back through the forest slow.
data.secretGems.tzelefos-dawn.title: Tzelefos at dawn
data.secretGems.vasilikon-akamas.body: Kathikas sits at 650–700m on the Akamas–Laona edge. Do Adonis or Aphrodite trail in the morning, Polis harbour for lunch, then Vasilikon on the loop back. Their Xynisteri has PDO status; Ayios Onoufrios is the flagship red. No appointment needed—Mon–Sun 8:30–18:00. The cellar, museum, and terrace overlook the Akamas. Cheese platters with tastings. Quieter than Omodos.
data.secretGems.vasilikon-akamas.title: Vasilikon: on the Akamas loop
data.secretGems.vavla-quiet-escape.body: Between Larnaca and Troodos. No lace, no wine route fame. Just quiet lanes, olive groves, and guesthouses that offer silence. In winter you might be the only visitor. The village sits in a fold of the hills. Walk the streets. Find the kafenion. The pace is slow. It's the kind of place where you stay one night and wish for two. Use it as a base for Lefkara, Choirokoitia, or the Troodos. Or don't. Just be there.
data.secretGems.vavla-quiet-escape.title: Vavla: the village nobody mentions
data.secretGems.vlassides-rainbow.body: Sophocles Vlassides studied at UC Davis; the winery was shortlisted for the Mies van der Rohe Award. The Rainbow tasting (€7.50) pours three wines; the 4×4 (€18) pairs four wines with four cheeses. Book at least a day ahead. Koilani village, Krasochoria. Their Shiraz and Cabernet are standouts—fruit-forward, minimal oak. The building itself is worth seeing.
data.secretGems.vlassides-rainbow.title: Vlassides: the Rainbow tasting
data.secretGems.vouni-panayia-commandari: Ask for a comparative Commandaria tasting—younger and older vintages side by side. You'll taste what time does to the wine. The museum and film add context. Panayia village church has a revered icon; locals combine a quick stop. Winter hours 9–4. Combine with Pafos mosaics or Polis for a full Laona day.
data.secretGems.vretsia-early-start.body: Evacuated village, forest trail to Roudias bridge. Remote. Start by 9am in winter—light is short. Tell someone your route. The watermill ruins halfway. The bridge at the end. Worth it. Not a casual stroll.
data.secretGems.zambartas-aes-ambelis.bo: Twenty minutes from Limassol. Do both in one afternoon. Zambartas first—clean, modern, the Lefkada is a flagship. Then Aes Ambelis next door. Compare styles. The drive between is nothing. The winemakers know each other. They'll tell you. Two estates, one trip.
data.secretGems.zambartas-winemaker.body: Book the Winemaker's Selection (€20)—it's the one that includes an exclusive barrel sample of their Commandaria. Marcos Zambartas still leads tastings when he's in. The platter—halloumi, lountza, fruit, bread with organic olive oil—pairs well. Twenty-five minutes from Limassol. Do Kourion or Kolossi in the morning; Zambartas in the afternoon. Winter hours: Mon–Fri to 5pm, weekends to 6pm.
data.secretGems.zambartas-winemaker.titl: Zambartas: ask for the barrel sample
data.secretGems.zygi-fish-tavernas.body: Between Larnaca and Limassol. No ruins, no lace. Just fish. The tavernas line the harbour; they serve what the boats brought in that morning. Locals eat here. Tourists rarely find it. Winter lunch on the waterfront—octopus, sea bream, calamari. The pace is slow. The coffee after is obligatory. Combine with Kiti and the Angeloktisti church, or Choirokoitia. Zygi is where Cypriots go for Sunday fish. You should too.
data.secretGems.zygi-fish-tavernas.title: Zygi: the fishing village
data.secretGems.zygi-sunday.body: Between Larnaca and Limassol. No ruins, no lace. Just fish. The tavernas line the harbour; they serve what the boats brought in. Sunday is locals' day. Octopus, sea bream, calamari. The pace is slow. The coffee after is obligatory. Combine with Choirokoitia or Lefkara. Tourists rarely find it.
data.secretGems.zygi-sunday.title: Zygi: where Cypriots go for fish

data.trails.adonis.description: Winter Akamas favorite. Official Forestry Adonis Trail is about 7.5 km circular from the Baths of Aphrodite (grade 2, ~3 hours). Shares the first ~2.5 km with Aphrodite toward Pyrgos tis Rigainas, then continues via Kefalovrysia and Queen's Tower. Rocky and uphill early. December and January: ideal temps. Combine with Vasilikon (Akamas loop) or Chrysorrogiatissa and Kolios (Paphos hills).
data.trails.adonis.localSecret: Refill at Kefalovrysia spring. The Baths of Aphrodite café at the trailhead does a good post-hike coffee. Combine with Kolios or Vasilikon winery on the loop back.
data.trails.adonis.name: Adonis Trail
data.trails.adonis.waypoints.0.name: Baths of Aphrodite
data.trails.adonis.waypoints.1.name: Kefalovrysia spring
data.trails.adonis.waypoints.2.name: Queen's Tower ruins
data.trails.adonis.waypoints.3.name: Return via coast
data.trails.adonis.winterNotes: Best season for this trail. Cool temps, fewer crowds. Some muddy patches after rain.
data.trails.adonis.winterSafety: Winter is ideal; avoid summer heat. Some muddy patches after rain. Stay on marked path; Akamas has unexploded ordnance in places.
data.trails.agia-irini.description: Dramatic gorge in the Paphos forest. Rocky terrain, endemic flora. Allow four hours. Winter: cooler, ideal for hiking. The gorge narrows in places; spectacular. Combine with Polis, Latsi, or the Akamas trails. Point-to-point; arrange transport. One of Cyprus's finest gorge walks.
data.trails.agia-irini.localSecret: One of Cyprus's finest gorges. Narrow sections, endemic plants. Arrange transport.
data.trails.agia-irini.name: Agia Irini Gorge
data.trails.agia-irini.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Cool, shaded. Rocky underfoot.
data.trails.agia-tilliria.description: Distinct from the rest of Cyprus. Kato Pyrgos area—abandoned village of Agios Theodoros, wooden bridge, gorge views, shimmering Mediterranean in the distance. The landscape rises sharply; it feels like Crete. Remote; reach via Nicosia or Paphos. Linear or circular. Winter brings crisp air. Totally worth the drive.
data.trails.agia-tilliria.localSecret: Walk the asphalt back for a circular route. The sea view from the forest is rare in Cyprus.
data.trails.agia-tilliria.name: Agia Tilliria
data.trails.agia-tilliria.winterNotes: Cool and quiet. The area feels different—more remote.
data.trails.agia-varvara-stavrovouni.des: Short but brutal. Steep ascent from Agia Varvara Monastery to Stavrovouni peak. 280 m gain in 2.4 km. Rocky, sometimes very steep. Rewards: panoramic views of Larnaca, Salt Lake, coastline. Thirty minutes from Larnaca. Combine with Stavrovouni loop for ~10 km. Good training ground.
data.trails.agia-varvara-stavrovouni.loc: Park at Agia Varvara if trailhead lot is full. Combine with Stavrovouni loop for a full workout.
data.trails.agia-varvara-stavrovouni.tra: Agia Varvara Monastery, a few hundred metres after on left
data.trails.agia-varvara-stavrovouni.win: Avoid wooden steps when wet—slippery. Best in dry conditions.
data.trails.agioi-anargyroi-circular.des: Official Cape Greco circular: 4.8 km, about 2 hours, grade 1. Start at Konnos beach, Agioi Anargyroi church, or the Visitor Centre. Coastal scrub to the church over a sea cave, then Kamara tou Koraka natural bridge and Aphrodite temple ruins. Juniper, wild olive, carob. Part of the E4. Year-round winter sun classic.
data.trails.agioi-anargyroi-circular.loc: Three start points—park at whichever is quietest. Pair with Kavos or Cyclops for a full park day.
data.trails.agioi-anargyroi-circular.tra: Konnos beach, Agioi Anargyroi church, or Cape Greco Visitor Centre
data.trails.agioi-anargyroi-circular.win: Ideal winter walk. Mild. Quieter than summer. Year-round per official guide.
data.trails.almirolivado.description: The king of winter trails. A seasonal lake appears only after heavy rain or snow—few know it exists. The route passes an abandoned asbestos mine with lunar-like terrain, then descends to the secret lake. Go anticlockwise to reach the lake earlier. Best in winter when Troodos is dusted with snow. Go with someone who knows the route; it's hiker-made, not officially marked.
data.trails.almirolivado.localSecret: Go with someone who knows it. The lake appears only after snow or rain. Detour to the giant juniper adds 1 km and is worth it.
data.trails.almirolivado.name: Almirolivado Secret Lake
data.trails.almirolivado.winterNotes: Best in winter. Lake appears only after snow or heavy rain. Slippery when icy.
data.trails.almirolivado.winterSafety: Sections can be slippery when icy. Do not attempt alone. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.aphrodite-cape-greco.descrip: Official Cape Greco circular: 2 km, about 1 hour, grade 1. Starts at the Visitor Centre parking—distinct from the Akamas Aphrodite Trail. Down to the shore, links Sea Caves–Agioi Anargyroi, then up past Aphrodite temple ruins and shepherd cave walls. Views toward Pedalio lighthouse. Cypria Aphrodite cultural route and E4 sections. Year-round.
data.trails.aphrodite-cape-greco.localSe: Short loop that stitches into Sea Caves and Konnos–Agioi Anargyroi. Best light late afternoon on limestone.
data.trails.aphrodite-cape-greco.name: Aphrodite Trail (Cape Greco)
data.trails.aphrodite-cape-greco.trailhe: Cape Greco Visitor Centre parking (via Agioi Anargyroi turn from Agia Napa–Protaras)
data.trails.aphrodite-cape-greco.winterN: Ideal winter walk. Mild. Year-round per official guide. Not the Akamas Aphrodite Trail.
data.trails.aphrodite.description: Official Forestry Aphrodite Trail is about 7.5 km circular from the Baths of Aphrodite (grade 2, ~3 hours). Shares the early stretch with Adonis, then climbs toward Moutti tis Sotiras with Chrysochou Bay views. Winter is ideal—mild coast, wildflowers Feb–Mar. Pack a wind layer for the ridge.
data.trails.aphrodite.localSecret: Moutti tis Sotiras is the high point. Stop there. The bay views open out. The Baths of Aphrodite café awaits when you're done. You've earned it.
data.trails.aphrodite.name: Aphrodite Trail
data.trails.aphrodite.waypoints.0.name: Baths of Aphrodite
data.trails.aphrodite.waypoints.1.name: Moutti tis Sotiras (~370m)
data.trails.aphrodite.waypoints.2.name: Descent through forest
data.trails.aphrodite.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Mild coast temps. Wildflowers Feb to Mar.
data.trails.aphrodite.winterSafety: Ideal winter coastal hike. Cool temps, wildflowers Feb to Mar. Carry wind layer; exposed ridge.
data.trails.ariadni.description: Circular trail near Gerakies, a few hundred metres from the Kykkos road. Steep start to Kavallos fire lookout; then ridgeline walking with panoramic views of Paphos forest and Marathasa Valley. On clear days: Pentadaktylos, Morphou Bay. Best in winter—most of the trail is exposed. Combine with Rigaina's Baths for a full day.
data.trails.ariadni.localSecret: Cloudy days make the ridgeline comfortable. Gerakies village for a post-hike stop.
data.trails.ariadni.name: Ariadni Natural Trail
data.trails.ariadni.winterNotes: Best in winter. Exposed ridgelines; summer sun is harsh.
data.trails.artemis.description: Winter Troodos favorite. Seven-kilometre loop around Chionistra (Mount Olympus) at about 1,850 m through Troodos National Forest Park. Black pine, golden oak, ridge views. Forestry Department grade 1—smooth path, little climb. In winter the air is crisp, the crowds thin. Well-marked; weather changes fast—pack layers.
data.trails.artemis.localSecret: Start anti-clockwise; the eastern section has the best views and you hit them before lunch. Quietest on weekday mornings.
data.trails.artemis.name: Artemis Trail
data.trails.artemis.trailhead: 300 m from the Chionistra road junction on the Troodos–Prodromos road (parking at start)
data.trails.artemis.waypoints.0.name: Trailhead (Chionistra junction)
data.trails.artemis.waypoints.1.name: Eastern ridge
data.trails.artemis.waypoints.2.name: Black pine forest
data.trails.artemis.waypoints.3.name: Western descent
data.trails.artemis.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November as most suitable; winter is doable when clear of ice. Can be icy after cold snaps; check conditions before starting.
data.trails.artemis.winterSafety: After cold snaps, higher sections can be icy. Carry microspikes if forecast is near freezing. Troodos Visitor Centre posts conditions. Phone signal patchy; tell someone your route.
data.trails.atalante.description: Full Troodos day hike. Official Forestry Atalanti Trail is a 14 km loop from Troodos Square around Chionistra, lower than Artemis—dense black pine and Troodos juniper (including an ~800-year-old specimen). Grade 2; about five hours. Drinking water about 3 km in; old chromium mine entrance near 5 km. Cross the Troodos–Prodromos road near 9 km and follow signs back to the square. Start early; pack lunch.
data.trails.atalante.localSecret: Do Artemis and Atalante on different days. Combining both is a very long outing; the shared Chionistra circuit is the link.
data.trails.atalante.name: Atalante Trail
data.trails.atalante.waypoints.0.name: Troodos Square
data.trails.atalante.waypoints.1.name: Drinking fountain
data.trails.atalante.waypoints.2.name: Chromium mine entrance
data.trails.atalante.waypoints.3.name: Troodos–Prodromos road
data.trails.atalante.waypoints.3.note: Cross road; follow forest track signs
data.trails.atalante.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November as most suitable; winter only when ice-free. Longer than Artemis—start early.
data.trails.atalante.winterSafety: Long loop—do not underestimate. Ice after cold snaps; microspikes if needed. Tell someone your route. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.avakas-gorge.description: Avakas Gorge is a slot in the limestone. Official Forestry route is about 1.2 km linear into the gorge (grade 1–2, allow ~2 hours with care). Walls rise high on either side; river crossings and slip risk. Centauria akamantis grows here. Do not go after heavy rain—flash floods are real. December–April when the river is manageable. Waterproof boots; some scrambling.
data.trails.avakas-gorge.localSecret: The narrowest point is where the sky becomes a strip. Go slow. Avakas Winery nearby; combine gorge walk with a tasting. Call ahead.
data.trails.avakas-gorge.name: Avakas Gorge
data.trails.avakas-gorge.winterNotes: Check weather; avoid after rain. Gorge can be slippery. Best Dec to Apr when river is manageable.
data.trails.avakas-gorge.winterSafety: Do NOT enter after heavy rain; flash flood risk. Gorge can be slippery. Best Dec to Apr when river is low. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.caledonia-alternative.descri: The long route. Eleven kilometres from Platres to Troodos, passing Caledonia Falls along the way. You walk the length of the Kryos Potamos valley; the Cold River; through forest that feels ancient. The waterfall is the midpoint. Stop. Rest. Then push on. It's a point-to-point hike, so you need transport at both ends. Arrange a car or a lift. Allow six hours. Muddy sections after rain. Snow possible at the Troodos end in deep winter. Start early. Pack lunch. This is a full day in the mountains. Fit hikers only. But if you're up for it, the Caledonia Long Route is one of the island's best walks.
data.trails.caledonia-alternative.localS: Caledonia Falls at km 4 is the midpoint. Stop there. Rest. The waterfall is the reward before the push to Troodos. Arrange your lift before you start.
data.trails.caledonia-alternative.name: Caledonia Long Route
data.trails.caledonia-alternative.winter: Muddy sections. Snow possible at Troodos end. Start early.
Point-to-point: arrange transport. Muddy sections; snow possible at Troodos end. Full-day hike; start early.
data.trails.caledonia-falls.description: Best winter waterfall hike. Official Forestry route is about 3 km linear between Troodos (above) and Psilo Dentro above Pano Platres, along Kryos Potamos. Grade 2–3: stream crossings, slippery stones. Flow peaks in late winter; forest green, air cool. Waterproof boots. Ask in Platres about rainfall.
data.trails.caledonia-falls.localSecret: The falls are most impressive 1 to 2 days after rain. Check flow online or ask at Platres cafés.
data.trails.caledonia-falls.name: Caledonia Falls
data.trails.caledonia-falls.trailhead: 500 m below Troodos Square toward Platres, or Psilo Dentro (Pano Platres)
Park at Psilo Dendro; follow Kryos Potamos
Rocks may be slippery after rain
data.trails.caledonia-falls.winterNotes: Muddy sections after rain. High slip risk at river crossings. Wear waterproof boots. Waterfall flow peaks in late winter/spring.
data.trails.caledonia-falls.winterSafety: Slippery rocks near the falls. Stay on the path. Stream can rise quickly after rain; do not attempt in storm conditions. Trail can be muddy; waterproof boots essential.
data.trails.cape-aspro.description: White cliffs, endless blue. Pissouri—a coastal hike unlike any forest trail. Steepest white cliffs in Cyprus, ~250 m. The path runs a few metres back from the edge; safe but dramatic. No shade—best in winter. Linear out-and-back. Start near Columbia Beach hotel. Different kind of hike.
data.trails.cape-aspro.localSecret: Narrow section at start—passable but careful. The combination of cliffs and sea is unforgettable.
data.trails.cape-aspro.name: Cape Aspro
data.trails.cape-aspro.winterNotes: Ideal in winter. No shade at all. Cloudy days add drama.
data.trails.cape-greco.description: Six kilometres along the Cape Greco coast. Sea caves, limestone cliffs, coves where the water shifts from turquoise to deep blue. In winter the sun is mild and the path is quiet. No snow, no crowds. The trail is well-marked. You can start at the Cape Greco car park or at Konnos Bay. The sea is always on one side. The light changes with the hour. Bring a wind layer; the cliffs funnel the breeze. It's the kind of hike that feels like a gift: easy underfoot, views that don't quit. Combine with a swim in summer or a coffee at Konnos in winter.
data.trails.cape-greco.localSecret: Start at Konnos Bay and walk toward the sea caves. The light on the limestone is best in the afternoon. Combine with Konnos for a swim in summer or a coffee in winter.
data.trails.cape-greco.name: Cape Greco Coastal Path
data.trails.cape-greco.trailhead: Cape Greco car park or Konnos Bay
data.trails.cape-greco.waypoints.0.name: Cape Greco car park
data.trails.cape-greco.waypoints.1.name: Sea caves
data.trails.cape-greco.waypoints.2.name: Lighthouse area
data.trails.cape-greco.waypoints.3.name: Konnos Bay (if out-and-back)
data.trails.cape-greco.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. No snow, mild temps. Good for escaping cold elsewhere.
data.trails.cape-greco.winterSafety: Ideal winter hike; mild, no snow. Coastal wind can be brisk; bring a layer. Path well-marked.
data.trails.chrysovrysi.description: Official Forestry linear: 8 km downhill in about 1 hour, grade 2 (1,315–1,050 m). Historic path villagers used toward the Amiantos asbestos mine. Starts ~300 m from Chrysovrysi stone fountain on the Karvounas–Troodos road—fill bottles before you go. Dense Calabrian pine, golden oak, gabbro of the Troodos ophiolite; last stretch on a dirt farm road into Amiantos. Natura 2000. Arrange transport at Amiantos.
data.trails.chrysovrysi.localSecret: Fill canteens at Chrysovrysi. End near Amiantos Botanical Garden / Geopark Visitor Centre.
data.trails.chrysovrysi.name: Chrysovrysi Natural Trail
data.trails.chrysovrysi.trailhead: Karvounas–Troodos road, ~300 m from Chrysovrysi fountain (~1.2 km after Karvounas crossing)
data.trails.chrysovrysi.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November. Downhill linear—arrange a lift at Amiantos. Spring water at the start.
data.trails.dwarf-oaks.description: Short loop through golden oak and black pine. Easy grade; one hour. Endemic flora. Family-friendly. Winter: often clear; good for a gentle morning. Combine with Platres, Kykkos road, or other Troodos trails.
data.trails.dwarf-oaks.localSecret: Golden oak, black pine. Short and gentle. Ideal for a soft start.
data.trails.dwarf-oaks.name: Dwarf Oaks Trail
data.trails.dwarf-oaks.winterNotes: Often clear. Gentle. Good for families.
data.trails.e4-troodos-platres.descripti: A section of the E4 European Long Distance Walk. From Platres through forest to the Caledonia Falls area. Pine, golden oak, mountain views. The E4 crosses Cyprus from coast to coast; this segment gives a taste of long-distance hiking. Allow four hours. Winter: check conditions; can be snowy at higher points. Combine with Platres for lunch or a second shorter trail.
data.trails.e4-troodos-platres.localSecr: A taste of the full E4. Fit hikers can tag Caledonia Falls as a detour. Platres for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.e4-troodos-platres.name: E4 Troodos Section (Platres–Caledonia)
data.trails.e4-troodos-platres.winterNot: Check conditions; snow possible at elevation. Often clear in December or March.
data.trails.germasogeia-kyparissia.descr: Circular route from Foinikaria. Pine forest, Germasogeia reservoir, climb to Kyparissia Peak (~760 m). Views to the coast. Birdlife: coal tits, goldfinches, buzzards. Krasochoria wine route nearby. No water on route—bring plenty. Winter: cool and pleasant.
data.trails.germasogeia-kyparissia.local: Krasochoria wineries nearby. Combine with a tasting for a full Limassol day.
data.trails.germasogeia-kyparissia.name: Germasogeia Dam – Kyparissia
data.trails.germasogeia-kyparissia.winte: Cool and pleasant. No shade in sections—winter is ideal.
data.trails.gnafkio.description: Probably the greenest trail in Cyprus. Kampos and Tsakistras area—moss-covered path, dense vegetation, towering trees. First leg: narrow descent through forest; second leg: gravel road with Troodos views. Linear; can do one-way with a car at each end. Secluded. Winter adds snow on the peaks. Best in February for the moss.
data.trails.gnafkio.localSecret: Start from Kykkos–Tsakistra for steep descent first. Near Gnafkio trailhead is Panthea.
data.trails.gnafkio.name: Gnafkio Natural Trail
data.trails.gnafkio.trailhead: Kykkos toward Tsakistra, or Kykkos Water Plant road
data.trails.gnafkio.winterNotes: Winter brings snow on Troodos. The moss and green are stunning.
data.trails.horteri-extended.description: Extended loop in the Troodos forest, north of Platres. Pine, streams, mountain quiet. Slightly longer than the short Horteri option. Good for a half-day when you want more than a leg-stretcher but less than Artemis. Winter: check conditions; can be cool at elevation. Platres for trout after. Combine with Caledonia Falls or Kampos tou Livadiou for a full mountain day.
data.trails.horteri-extended.localSecret: Quieter than Artemis. More than a leg-stretcher. Platres trout rewards.
data.trails.horteri-extended.name: Horteri Extended Loop
data.trails.horteri-extended.winterNotes: Cool at elevation. Often clear. Platres nearby for warmth.
data.trails.horteri.description: The Horteri Trail is the one for experienced hikers. Nine kilometres through Troodos forest. Steep sections, rocky terrain, long stretches of solitude. You climb, dip, and climb again. The reward is views and silence. In winter, snow can settle on the higher points from January to March. Microspikes are often essential. Start early. Tell someone your route. The forest swallows you. Phone signal is patchy. But if you're fit and prepared, Horteri delivers. You'll earn your village lunch.
data.trails.horteri.localSecret: The solitude is the reward. You'll see few people. The forest ridge has moments of pure quiet. Earn your Platres lunch.
data.trails.horteri.name: Horteri Trail
data.trails.horteri.waypoints.0.name: Troodos Square start
data.trails.horteri.waypoints.1.name: Forest ridge
data.trails.horteri.waypoints.2.name: High point
data.trails.horteri.waypoints.3.name: Return loop
data.trails.horteri.winterNotes: Snow possible Jan to Mar. Microspikes may be needed. Start early.
data.trails.horteri.winterSafety: For experienced hikers only. Snow likely Jan to Mar at elevation. Microspikes essential. Tell someone your route. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.kalidonia-alt.description: Alternative approach to the Caledonia Falls area. Different start; same waterfall reward. Forest, stream, cooler temps. Allow two hours. Winter: muddy sections possible; waterproof boots. Platres for lunch.
data.trails.kalidonia-alt.localSecret: Different path to the same falls. Forest, stream. Platres warms you after.
data.trails.kalidonia-alt.name: Kalidonia Alternative Route
data.trails.kalidonia-alt.winterNotes: Muddy sections possible. Waterproof boots. Falls reward.
data.trails.kampos-tou-livadiou.descript: Official Forestry circular: 3 km, about 1.5 hours, grade 1. Cliff-edge views of Chromium River, Solea Valley, Morphou Bay, and the tip of Chionistra through black pine and century-old junipers. First kilometre shared with Mnimata Piskopon. Endemic flora signs (Cyprus skullcap, Troodos Alyson, golden oak). Natura 2000 Troodos National Forest Park. Quiet winter leg-stretcher; picnic site nearby.
data.trails.kampos-tou-livadiou.localSec: The Solea Valley view opens up halfway round. Quieter than Artemis and Atalante. Combine with Platres trout tavernas.
data.trails.kampos-tou-livadiou.name: Kampos tou Livadiou
data.trails.kampos-tou-livadiou.trailhea: Road to Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (kiosk ~100 m along the spur from Karvounas–Troodos)
data.trails.kampos-tou-livadiou.winterNo: Official guide lists March–November as most suitable; often clear when higher trails have snow. Watch forest-road junctions at the start.
data.trails.kannoures-agios-nikolaos.des: Official Forestry linear: 9 km downhill, about 3.5 hours, grade 3 (1,655–870 m). From Karvounas–Troodos road (~1 km before Troodos Square) via closed chromium mine at Kannoures, then along Karkotis River crossings on wet stones. Ends at UNESCO Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis beside the bottling plant. Black pine to Calabrian pine. Natura 2000.
data.trails.kannoures-agios-nikolaos.loc: Finish at Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis; continue 3 km by road into Kakopetria’s old neighbourhood.
data.trails.kannoures-agios-nikolaos.tra: Karvounas–Troodos road, ~9.5 km from Karvounas / 1 km before Troodos Square
data.trails.kannoures-agios-nikolaos.win: Official guide lists March–November. Frequent river crossings—high slip risk after rain. Arrange transport at Kakopetria.
data.trails.karvounarka.description: Circular trail from Vavatsinia—one of Larnaca's highest villages—through Machairas forest. First leg: nature path, dense forest, panoramic views (Limassol south, Morphou north). Second leg: paved road back. Can combine with Moutti tis Athasias for +4.4 km. Winter fog adds a mystic quality.
data.trails.karvounarka.localSecret: Combine with Moutti tis Athasias for the cave. Vavatsinia restaurants for lunch.
data.trails.karvounarka.name: Karvounarka
data.trails.karvounarka.trailhead: Vavatsinia–Kionia road, or Vavatsinia village centre
data.trails.karvounarka.winterNotes: Winter fog adds atmosphere. Second leg on road—exposed in summer.
data.trails.kavos-trail.description: Official Cape Greco circular: 1.2 km, about 45 minutes, grade 1. Starts at the old quarry car park; slight climb to Kavos hill then loop down. Pine then juniper and lentisk scrub; panoramic views to Pedalio lighthouse, Agia Napa, and the south cliffs (rock climbing). Connects to Sea Caves–Agioi Anargyroi. Year-round winter sun option.
data.trails.kavos-trail.localSecret: Less crowded than Cyclops. Pair with Sea Caves–Agioi Anargyroi for a longer coastal day.
data.trails.kavos-trail.name: Kavos Trail
data.trails.kavos-trail.trailhead: Old quarry, Cape Greco National Forest Park (unpaved spur to Kavos hill)
data.trails.kavos-trail.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk. Mild, coastal. Steep rocky cliffs on the south side—stay on path.
data.trails.kionia-profitis-elias.descri: E4 European long-distance trail through Machairas Forest. Kionia picnic site (1,240 m) or Profitis Elias (700 m)—start from either. Pine, golden oak, historic charcoal kilns, abandoned 12th-century monastery. Views of Larnaca and Nicosia. One of Cyprus's most beautiful trails. Winter: crisp air, fewer people.
data.trails.kionia-profitis-elias.localS: Start from Kionia for downhill to Profitis Elias. Arrange car at both ends.
data.trails.kionia-profitis-elias.name: Kionia – Profitis Elias
data.trails.kionia-profitis-elias.trailh: Kionia picnic site or Profitis Elias (Lythrodontas)
data.trails.kionia-profitis-elias.winter: Ideal winter hike. Cool forest. Profitis Elias start needs 5 km dirt road.
data.trails.kionia.description: Forest trail in the Troodos. Pine, ridges. Moderate grade. Allow two and a half hours. Winter: crisp; check conditions. Combine with Platres, Caledonia, or Kampos tou Livadiou. A solid half-day option.
data.trails.kionia.localSecret: Solid half-day. Forest and ridges. Platres trout.
data.trails.kionia.name: Kionia Nature Trail
data.trails.konnoi-cyclops.description: Official Cape Greco circular: 1.7 km, about 45 minutes, grade 1. From Konnos beach parking along the rugged shore to Spilia tou Kyklopa (Cyclops Cave), then return via beach path. Turquoise Konnos and Agioi Anargyroi views. Part of the E4. Year-round classic.
data.trails.konnoi-cyclops.localSecret: Café and water sports at Konnos. Pair with Agioi Anargyroi loop for a fuller park morning.
data.trails.konnoi-cyclops.name: Konnos – Cyclops Cave
data.trails.konnoi-cyclops.trailhead: Konnos beach parking (signposted from Agia Napa–Protaras / Cape Greco road)
data.trails.konnoi-cyclops.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk. Mild, no snow. Year-round per official guide.
data.trails.kryos-potamos-loop.descripti: The Cold River valley. A forest walk along the Kryos Potamos, the stream that feeds Caledonia Falls. Less demanding than the full Caledonia Long Route; good for a half-day in the mountains. Pine, moss, the sound of water. Winter brings crisp air. Can be combined with a shorter visit to the falls. Platres for lunch. Start from Psilo Dendro or the Caledonia trailhead.
data.trails.kryos-potamos-loop.localSecr: The stream, the moss, the forest. A gentler taste of the Caledonia valley. Psilo Dendro for trout after.
data.trails.kryos-potamos-loop.name: Kryos Potamos Valley Walk
data.trails.kryos-potamos-loop.winterNot: Muddy after rain. Wear waterproof boots. Winter flow in the stream is strong.
data.trails.kykkos-konizi.description: Hidden and unknown. Next to Kykkos Monastery, this trail dives into unspoiled Paphos forest. V-shaped: steep descent, streams at the bottom, steep ascent to Konizi. Dense forest, panoramic views, streams. Do not hike alone. Winter preferred—snakes in warm months. Very difficult; rocky, slippery in rain. Six hours for 14 km round trip.
data.trails.kykkos-konizi.localSecret: At 5 km, old gravel road—go right at water tank. Left at curve, not right. Very few know this trail.
data.trails.kykkos-konizi.name: Kykkos to Konizi
data.trails.kykkos-konizi.winterNotes: Best in winter. Avoid rain. Snakes less active. Do not go alone.
data.trails.kykkos-konizi.winterSafety: Do not hike alone. Snakes possible in warm months. Signal patchy. Tell someone your route.
data.trails.larnaca-salt-lake.descriptio: Flat circuit around Larnaca Salt Lake. Flamingos in winter; Hala Sultan Tekke mosque; birdlife. Easy, flat. Allow two hours. Winter: ideal for flamingos. Combine with Larnaca town, Kiti, or the airport corridor. A coastal wetlands escape.
data.trails.larnaca-salt-lake.localSecre: Flamingos, salt, mosque. Flat. Winter is peak bird season.
data.trails.larnaca-salt-lake.name: Larnaca Salt Lake Circuit
data.trails.larnaca-salt-lake.winterNote: Flamingos in winter. Flat, easy. Ideal for birdwatchers.
data.trails.lefkara-path.description: Village-to-village walk linking Pano and Kato Lefkara. Stone paths, lace workshops, mountain views. Easy grade. Combine with Lefkara lace, Choirokoitia, or Zygi for fish. Winter: mild; the villages are quieter. Culture and gentle exercise.
data.trails.lefkara-path.localSecret: Lace and stone. Village to village. Zygi for fish after.
data.trails.lefkara-path.name: Lefkara Villages Path
data.trails.lefkara-path.winterNotes: Mild in winter. Villages quieter. Culture and walk.
data.trails.livadi-trail.description: Official wheelchair-accessible circular: 1.5 km, about 30 minutes, grade 1. Gravel path through black pine and juniper near Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (not Troodos Square). Viewpoint over Chromium River and Solea Valley; century-old trees; flora signs. Natura 2000. Ideal for families and first-timers.
data.trails.livadi-trail.localSecret: Short and sweet. Pair with Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site. Ideal for first-timers or families.
data.trails.livadi-trail.name: Livadi Trail
data.trails.livadi-trail.trailhead: Narrow asphalt road to Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (~300 m toward the army camp from the spur junction)
data.trails.livadi-trail.winterNotes: Official guide lists April–October as most suitable; often clear when higher trails have snow. Good for families.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.descriptio: Official Forestry linear: 2.5 km, about 1 hour, grade 2. Valley of the Eagles between about 1,110 m and 1,010 m. Smooth path through pine forest near Amiantos; river crossings when water is up. Short characterful leg-stretcher. Arrange transport for the linear route.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.localSecre: Valley of the Eagles. Short but characterful. Pair with Chrysovrysi or Amiantos Botanical Garden.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.name: Loumata ton Aeton
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.trailhead: Amiantos–SEK Camping Site road (kiosk after Amiantos bridge turn)
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.winterNote: Official guide lists April–November; winter river levels rise—risk of slipping at crossings. Linear—arrange transport.
data.trails.machairas-forest.description: Forest trail around Machairas Monastery. Pine and golden oak; mountain views. The monastery sits at 870m. The trail winds through the surrounding forest. Moderate grade; allow three hours. Winter: crisp air, fewer visitors. Combine with the monastery, Agros, or a Nicosia hinterland day. About an hour from Nicosia. The monastery café does a good post-hike coffee.
data.trails.machairas-forest.localSecret: The monastery is the centrepiece. Forest trail, mountain air. Agros for loukoumi and rose products after.
data.trails.machairas-forest.name: Machairas Forest Trail
data.trails.machairas-forest.winterNotes: Good winter hike. Monastery at 870m; wrap up. Often clear when Troodos has snow.
data.trails.madari-ridge.description: Eight kilometres along the Madari Ridge. When the day is clear, 360° views over Pitsilia and Troodos. The fire watchtower marks the high point. Pine forest, open ridges, a stretch of the E4 long-distance trail. In winter the ridge can be windy. Snow sometimes settles in January and February. Check the forecast. On clear days the coast stretches out. A misty one still has its atmosphere; the forest closes in, the tower emerges from the cloud. Allow four or five hours. Bring layers. The ridge exposes you.
data.trails.madari-ridge.localSecret: The fire watchtower at km 2.5. Climb it if you can. The 360° views are worth the extra steps. Kyperounta Winery is nearby—among Europe's highest wineries. Combine if you have time.
data.trails.madari-ridge.name: Madari Ridge Walk
data.trails.madari-ridge.trailhead: Madari car park (Kyperounta to Spilia road)
data.trails.madari-ridge.winterNotes: Can be windy. Snow on ridge in Jan to Feb. On clear days the coast stretches out.
data.trails.madari-ridge.winterSafety: Ridge is exposed; wind chill significant. Snow possible Jan to Feb. 360° views on clear days. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.description: Unofficial loop near Moniatis. Waterfall cascading 7 m, cold river, Timiou Prodromou Monastery (15th century). Mostly dirt roads; family-friendly. Pine and walnut forest. Winter: mild; good for a capital escape. About 30 km from Limassol. Combine with Saittas or Krasochoria wineries.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.localSecret: From Limassol: Saittas road, Kato Amiantos. Look for waterfall signs. The monastery is the surprise.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.name: Mesa Potamos Waterfall
data.trails.mesa-potamos.winterNotes: Mild. Good winter option. Spring for peak flow.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.description: Millomeris is the gentler cousin of Caledonia Falls. Official Forestry route is about 1.2 km linear from Pano Platres (grade 1, ~45 minutes). Wooden walkways and steps; the waterfall drops about 20 metres—the tallest in Troodos. Strong flow after rain. Families manage it. Combine with coffee in Platres.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.localSecret: Do Millomeris in the morning, then Platres for lunch. The trout tavernas or a café by the river. It's a gentle half-day. Ideal when you don't want a full mountain push.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.name: Millomeris Falls
data.trails.millomeris-falls.trailhead: Pano Platres (signed from village, before Panagia tis Phaneromenis)
data.trails.millomeris-falls.winterNotes: Muddy after rain. Waterfall impressive in winter/spring. Frequent stream crossings—slip risk.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.winterSafet: Family-friendly. Wooden walkways can be slippery when wet. Waterfall flow peaks after rain. Shorter and easier than Caledonia.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.description: Official Forestry linear: 8 km, about 3 hours, grade 3. Starts near Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (first km shared with that circular); mostly downhill from ~1,700 m to ~980 m. Cliff-edge views of Chromium River, Solea Valley, Morphou Bay, and Chionistra. Black pine gives way to Calabrian pine below 1,400 m. Ends on the Platania–Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis forest road—continue to Kakopetria or Platania. Natura 2000. Arrange transport.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.localSecret: The first km is shared with Kampos tou Livadiou. Views from the cliff edges are the reward. Kakopetria for lunch at the end.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.name: Mnimata Piskopon
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.trailhead: Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site spur (Karvounas–Troodos road)
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November; can be snowy. Linear—arrange transport at both ends. Watch forest-road junctions at the start.
data.trails.moni-fylagra.description: Official Forestry linear: 3 km, about 1 hour, grade 2 (1,000–700 m). Between Pelendri (Trimiklini–Pelendri road) and Fylagra on the Saittas–Kato Amiantos road. Historic vineyard path; ~2 km private land, ~1 km Moni State Forest. Views to Limassol bay and Kourris Dam. Recovering Calabrian pine after the 2007 fire. Local winery ~250 m west near Fylagra.
data.trails.moni-fylagra.localSecret: Visit Timios Stavros in Pelendri (UNESCO) after. Krasochoria wineries nearby.
data.trails.moni-fylagra.name: Moni – Fylagra
data.trails.moni-fylagra.trailhead: Trimiklini–Pelendri road near Pelendri, or Fylagra settlement (Kato Amiantos–Fylagra)
data.trails.moni-fylagra.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November. Rocky sections—risk of slipping. Linear; allow 2 hours if returning the same way.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.description: Peak of Winds. A hidden gem in the remote Paphos forest. Linear trail from Pano Panagia toward Stavros tis Psokas; shares a trailhead with Gefyria. Ridgeline walking, 360° views, fewer visitors than Troodos. The Paphos forest feels wilder—more untamed. Check GPS near the end; one junction can lead astray.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.localSecret: Combine with Gefyria for a longer day. The Paphos forest has a different character to Troodos.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.name: Moutti twn Anemwn
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.trailhead: Pano Panagia, road toward Stavros tis Psokas
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.winterNotes: Quiet in winter. Windy on the peak—hence the name.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.description: A quiet path, chosen among locals. Near Vavatsinia, the trail follows a scenic forest road before narrowing into woodland. At the end: a mysterious cave—Venetian-era mine for gold and copper. Do not enter; it goes deep and is unmaintained. The cave marks the turnaround. Easy, beginner-friendly. Limited parking.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.localSecret: Chosen by locals, not tourists. Combine with Karvounarka for a longer loop.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.name: Moutti tis Athasias (Cave)
data.trails.moutti-athasias.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk. Cool forest. Cave is the reward.
data.trails.mylikouri.description: Forest trail near Kakopetria. Pine, streams, mountain air. Moderate grade. Allow two hours. Winter: crisp; often clear. Combine with Kakopetria trout tavernas, Kampos tou Livadiou, or Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis. A Solea Valley classic.
data.trails.mylikouri.localSecret: Solea Valley classic. Forest, streams. Kakopetria trout rewards.
data.trails.mylikouri.name: Mylikouri Nature Trail
data.trails.mylikouri.winterNotes: Crisp in winter. Often clear. Kakopetria for trout after.
data.trails.olympus-summit.description: Cyprus's highest peak. 1,952 metres. Winter: snow and ice common Jan–Mar. Microspikes needed. Steep ascent through black pine; 360-degree view on clear days. Start early; cloud builds by midday. Check conditions. Ski resort café at trailhead.
data.trails.olympus-summit.localSecret: On clear winter days you can see both coasts. Start early; cloud often builds by midday. Ski resort café for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.olympus-summit.name: Olympus Summit Trail
data.trails.olympus-summit.trailhead: Troodos Ski Resort / Charalambos the Goat Shepherd
data.trails.olympus-summit.waypoints.0.n: Park at Troodos Ski; check if road is open
data.trails.olympus-summit.winterNotes: Snow/ice common Jan to Mar. Microspikes recommended. Check resort status; ski area may restrict access.
data.trails.olympus-summit.winterSafety: Snow and ice common Jan to Mar. Microspikes or crampons often required. Check ski resort status; access may be restricted. Do not attempt in whiteout or high wind. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.descript: Easy loop in the Limassol hills. The trail passes the church of Panagia tis Amasgou and winds through olive groves and scrub. Gentle grade; family-friendly. Winter sun, mild temps. Combine with Monagri, Omodos, or a Krasochoria winery visit. A relaxed morning or afternoon option.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.localSec: Gentle, quiet. Olive groves and winter light. Krasochoria wineries nearby.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.name: Panagia tis Amasgou Trail
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.winterNo: Easy winter walk. Mild. Good for families.
data.trails.panthea.description: Remote ridge on the Kykkos–Tsakistra road. A refuge at the start—jewelry hidden in plain sight. First section: ridgeline with continuous views; then mountain peaks, gravel road toward Kampos or Tsakistra. Park at both ends for one-way, or out-and-back. Best in winter; cloudy days add atmosphere. Shares area with Gnafkio.
data.trails.panthea.localSecret: The refuge at the start is magical. Park cars at both ends for a one-way hike.
data.trails.panthea.name: Panthea Natural Trail
data.trails.panthea.winterNotes: Best in winter. Cloudy weather adds drama.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.description: Foothills of the Five Fingers mountain. Views of the coast and the range. Easy grade. Note: access from south Cyprus; check current routes. Combine with Bellapais, St Hilarion, or coastal Kyrenia. Winter: mild on the coast; the mountains frame the view.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.localSecret: Five Fingers. Coast and range. Bellapais abbey in view.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.name: Pentadaktylos Foothills
data.trails.pentadaktylos.winterNotes: Mild. Coast views. Check access. Bellapais and St Hilarion nearby.
data.trails.persephone-extended.descript: Extended variant of the Persephone trail. More distance, more forest. Troodos heartland. Moderate grade. Allow nearly three hours. Winter: check conditions; can be cool. Platres for lunch. Connects to the wider Troodos network.
data.trails.persephone-extended.localSec: More Persephone. Forest, mountain. Platres trout after.
data.trails.persephone-extended.name: Persephone Extended Loop
data.trails.persephone-extended.winterNo: Cool at elevation. Often clear. Platres nearby.
data.trails.persephone.description: Short Troodos classic. Official Persephone Trail runs about 3 km from near Troodos Square (police station side, ~1,720 m) to the Makria Kontarka viewpoint (~1,660 m)—linear, so return the same way or via the signed forest road. Grade 1. Dense black pine, endemic flora signs, views toward Limassol vineyards and Cape Gata on clear days. Quieter than Artemis.
data.trails.persephone.localSecret: Late Feb to early Mar: look for cyclamen and anemones in the clearings. Less crowded than Artemis.
data.trails.persephone.name: Persephone Trail
data.trails.persephone.trailhead: About 150 m south of Troodos Square (toward the police station)
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.0.name: Troodos Square start
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.1.name: Forest clearings
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.2.name: Makria Kontarka viewpoint
data.trails.persephone.winterNotes: Feb to Mar wildflowers in clearings. Can be icy after cold snaps; check conditions.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.description: A coastal walk that strings together one of Cyprus's most famous landmarks; Petra tou Romiou, Aphrodite's Rock; with quiet stretches of shoreline. You start near the viewpoint car park and follow paths and tracks that keep the sea in sight. In winter the light is softer, the crowds gone. Waves break on the rocks, the air smells of salt and wild thyme. The route is mostly easy underfoot, with one or two short climbs to low bluffs for better views along the coast toward Pissouri. It's a half-day option when the mountains feel too cold. Pair it with a village lunch inland or a visit to Kourion or the Pafos mosaics to round out the day.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.localSecret: Walk east toward the quieter coves once you've had your fill of Aphrodite's Rock. The low bluffs give better views for photos, especially late afternoon when the light drops behind you.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.name: Petra tou Romiou Coastal Walk
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.trailhead: Petra tou Romiou viewpoint car park, old Paphos to Limassol road
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.1: Famous landmark; rocky shore, strong currents
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.2: Low cliffs with long views toward Pissouri
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.3: Turnaround point; return the same way
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk; mild temperatures and fewer people. Waves can be stronger after storms; stay well back from the waterline on rough days.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.winterSafet: Do not swim here; currents are strong even on calm days. Stay back from the waterline in winter storms; rogue waves can reach higher than expected. Coastal wind can be brisk; bring a layer.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.description: Official Akamas circular from Smigies picnic site: 3 km, about 2 hours, Forestry grade 2. Climb to Pissouromoutti hill (about 400 m), then circle down. Views south to Lara and Geronisos, north over Chrysochou Bay. Juniper, lentisk, pine shade on warm days. Year-round; drinking water at the picnic site. Mythology ties the name to Adonis and Aphrodite’s night chase.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.localSecret: The summit views open out at the top. Combine with Smigies long route for a full morning. Polis for lunch.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.name: Pissouromoutti Trail
data.trails.pissouromoutti.trailhead: Smigies picnic site (via Neo Chorio and Agios Minas agricultural road)
data.trails.pissouromoutti.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Cool, shaded sections. Risk of slipping after rain.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.descripti: A hidden sanctuary. Gorge, stream, Grigoris Afxentiou hideout, Machairas Monastery. The path follows the Pediaios River through a vast ravine; a bridge halfway crosses the mountainside. Magical after rain—the stream runs strong, the forest turns vivid green. Linear; both ends accessible by car. Experienced hikers can extend to Lazanias or Fikardou.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.localSecr: Go after rain. The bridge crossing is the highlight. Machairas café for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.name: Politiko to Machairas
data.trails.politiko-machairas.winterNot: Winter is magic—stream flows, greenery. First half exposed; second half shaded.
data.trails.potamia-dam.description: Circular route around Potamia Dam. Water views, birdlife, gentle grade. Easy; suitable for all. About 40 minutes from Nicosia. Winter: mild; good for a capital escape. Combine with Agros, Machairas, or Nicosia old town.
data.trails.potamia-dam.localSecret: Dam, birds, water. Easy capital escape. Agros for loukoumi after.
data.trails.potamia-dam.name: Potamia Dam Trail
data.trails.potamia-dam.winterNotes: Mild. Good capital escape. Dam and water views.
data.trails.prodromos-dam-stavroulia.des: Official Forestry linear: about 5.2–5.5 km, 2 hours, grade 3 (1,600–1,300 m). Starts ~200 m after Prodromos Dam on the Prodromos–Troodos Square road. Steep downhill; risk of slipping. Ancient black pines (some 500+ years), flora signs, Natura 2000 Forestry College forest. Shares sections with Prodromos–Zoumi; two finishes toward Pedoulas–Kakopetria.
data.trails.prodromos-dam-stavroulia.loc: Pair with Prodromos–Zoumi for a fuller Marathasa day. Watch footing on the descent.
data.trails.prodromos-dam-stavroulia.tra: Prodromos–Troodos Square road, ~200 m after Prodromos Dam (parking opposite)
data.trails.prodromos-dam-stavroulia.win: Official guide lists March–November. Steep downhill—fit hikers only. Arrange transport.
data.trails.prodromos-zoumi.description: Official Forestry linear: about 6–6.2 km, 2.5 hours, grade 2 (1,500–1,300 m). Starts at the Department of Forests playground in Prodromos. First ~3 km uphill, then downhill to Zoumi with two finish options on the Pedoulas–Kakopetria road. Black pine, Marathasa and Morphou Bay views. Connects to Prodromos Dam–Stavroulia. Natura 2000.
data.trails.prodromos-zoumi.localSecret: At Zoumi you can continue on Prodromos Dam–Stavroulia. Prodromos taverns for lunch.
data.trails.prodromos-zoumi.name: Prodromos – Zoumi
data.trails.prodromos-zoumi.trailhead: Department of Forests playground, Prodromos (~100 m NE of village square)
data.trails.prodromos-zoumi.winterNotes: Official guide lists March–November. Risk of slipping. Linear—arrange transport.
data.trails.psilo-dentro-pouziaris.descr: Official Forestry circular: 9 km, about 4 hours, grade 3 (1,690–1,190 m). Starts on the Moniatis–Troodos road near Psilo Dentro (Pano Platres). Calabrian then black pine; views to Kourris Dam, Limassol, and wine villages. Tiring ups and downs throughout. Natura 2000 Troodos National Forest Park.
data.trails.psilo-dentro-pouziaris.local: Park at Psilo Dentro restaurant. Platres is metres away for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.psilo-dentro-pouziaris.name: Psilo Dentro – Pouziaris
data.trails.psilo-dentro-pouziaris.trail: Pano Platres–Mesa Potamos forest road, ~50 m before Psilo Dentro restaurant (Moniatis–Troodos)
data.trails.psilo-dentro-pouziaris.winte: Official guide lists March–November. Risk of slipping. Fit hikers only.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.descript: Official Cape Greco linear: 4 km, about 1.5 hours, grade 1. Sea Caves to Agioi Anargyroi church (or reverse). Rocky shoreline, then scrub to Kamara tou Koraka natural bridge. E4 path. Connects to Konnos–Agioi Anargyroi and Aphrodite (Cape Greco) trails. Winter means fewer crowds.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.localSec: Don’t miss the windswept protected juniper after the Cape Greco turn. Picnic site west of the church.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.name: Sea Caves – Agioi Anargyroi
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.trailhea: Sea Caves or Church of Agioi Anargyroi (parking at both)
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.winterNo: Winter = fewer crowds. Mild. Ideal coastal walk. Year-round per official guide.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.description: Forest trail in the Troodos heartland. Pine, ridges, mountain views. Moderate grade; allow two and a half hours. Winter can bring snow at elevation; check conditions. Connects to the wider Troodos trail network. Platres or Kakopetria for lunch. A solid half-day in the mountains.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.localSecret: Quieter than Artemis. Ridge and forest. Platres for trout after.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.name: Selladi tis Stavros
data.trails.selladi-stavros.winterNotes: Check conditions; snow possible. Often clear in December or March.
